caption:
🔥 *Koffee With Karan* पर स्टार कपल्स की ट्रोलिंग पर आखिरकार शो के होस्ट करण जौहर का गुस्सा फूट ही पड़ा!

The Hollywood Reporter India को दिए एक इंटरव्यू में करण जौहर ने शो पर आने वाले रियल लाइफ कपल्स को जज करने वालों की जमकर क्लास लगाई। करण ने Ranveer Singh और Deepika Padukone का बचाव करते हुए कहा कि वे एक-दूसरे के प्यार में डूबे हुए बेहद खूबसूरत कपल हैं। उन्होंने कहा कि शो में वे सिर्फ अपनी जिंदगी को लेकर ईमानदार थे और किसी की ईमानदारी पर सवाल नहीं उठाए जाने चाहिए।

वहीं Vijay Deverakonda और Rashmika Mandanna के एपिसोड पर हुए विवाद पर करण बोले कि हर किसी को अपनी राय रखने का हक है, लेकिन किसी जोड़ी को यह बताने का हक नहीं कि उन्हें अपने रिश्ते में क्या करना चाहिए। करण ने ट्रोलर्स से तीखा सवाल पूछा, "आप कौन हैं? क्या आप कोई काउंसलर या वकील हैं?"

करण ने साफ कहा कि सेलेब्स पर राय रखो लेकिन उनके परिवारों को बीच में घसीटकर नीचा मत दिखाओ। उन्होंने कहा कि आज इंटरनेट पर clickbait और rage-bait का दौर है और लोग कमाई कर रहे हैं, लेकिन किसी को भी किसी कपल का endgame तय करने का हक नहीं है।

👇 आपकी इस बारे में क्या राय है, क्या लोग सोशल मीडिया पर कपल्स को जरूरत से ज्यादा जज करते हैं? कमेंट्स में बताओ!

ctx.text:
The filmmaker addresses the online backlash surrounding the episodes that featured real life couples like Ranveer – Deepika and Vijay – Rashmika.
Filmmaker and television host Karan Johar has addressed the online criticism surrounding the celebrity couple episodes of Koffee With Karan, particularly those featuring Ranveer Singh and Deepika Padukone in Season 8 and Vijay Deverakonda and Rashmika Mandanna in the latest season. In a conversation with The Hollywood Reporter India, Karan opened up about the trolling directed at the couples, expressing his reservations about audiences analysing their relationships and making unsolicited comments about their personal lives.
Recalling the backlash that followed the premiere episode of Koffee With Karan 8, which featured Ranveer Singh and Deepika Padukone together for the first time on the celebrity chat show, Karan maintained that the couple was simply being honest about their relationship. Defending their appearance, he said, “They are beautifully in love. Such good actors in love with each other.”
He further questioned why their candid conversation became a subject of judgement. “They were just being honest about their lives. Since when should honesty be judged? You should be appreciative of someone's honesty,” he said.
Karan also spoke about the criticism surrounding the Vijay Deverakonda and Rashmika Mandanna episode, which featured in the second episode of Koffee With Karan 9. Addressing the way viewers scrutinised the couple's interactions and relationship, the filmmaker said that while everyone was entitled to an opinion, there was a distinction between expressing an observation and attempting to dictate how two people should conduct their relationship.
“Everyone's entitled to an opinion. But when you start telling them what to do in that relationship, I have a very big problem,” he remarked. Questioning the sense of entitlement behind such commentary, he added, “Who are you? Are you a counsellor? Are you a lawyer? Are you a member of their family?”
The filmmaker also raised concerns about the involvement of celebrity families in online discussions. He pointed out that while public figures naturally attract opinions and scrutiny, their family members should not be dragged into conversations about their relationships. “You are commenting on their families. You can have an opinion on any celebrity. Don't demean their families. Their families weren't on that couch,” he said.
Reflecting on the culture of online commentary, Karan observed that every statement made on the show is now subjected to intense scrutiny, with individual lines often being taken apart and analysed. He acknowledged that digital platforms have created opportunities for content creators and publications to generate viewership through provocative headlines and opinions. However, he also maintained that everyone has a role to play in this ecosystem.
“At every given point of time, every line said is micro-analysed. If you want to, and if you think that your clickbait headline or your content piece about the show is going to get you a certain amount of viewership, that's also great,” he said.
Explaining his perspective on the changing digital landscape, Karan added, “You're doing your job and I'm doing mine. They're doing their job because the internet is now very monetizable. If your job means click-baiting something, rage-baiting something, and that is going to result in you earning from it, then it's fine. Or if you're just having an opinion, you're allowed [to]. It's a democratic nation."
Drawing a distinction between criticism and attempts to influence audience choices, Karan also shared his views on the larger culture of reviews and commentary. “I have no problem with a critic saying this is a bad film. I have a problem when they say don't watch it,” he explained.
